properties.name: fullonica (room 1)
properties.description: the fullery room in the north-west corner of the block, with the well and the two tubs, the work room of the small *fullonica* Amraoui describes in the north half of her *insula* 20 (Amraoui 2020b: 228-229, fig. 11.5); Ballu took the two workshops of this block for dyers (BCTH 1912: 494)

properties.name: fullonica (rooms 9 and 10)
properties.plan_source: Amraoui 2020b: 234, fig. 11.9; Christofle's plan in Wilson 2001: 275, fig. 12.04; round-2 drawing (Sep 29, 2026)
properties.description: the two fullery rooms on the north street, 9 and 10, with the three tubs, the well and the two compartments without tubs, c and e, the *fullonica* Amraoui puts in the north-east corner of her *insula* 19 on her plan and in her caption, in a unit of four rooms (9 to 12) with their own street doors (Amraoui 2020b: 233-234, fig. 11.9), though her text has east and west the other way round, and the two rooms Ballu says were filled by a well, two basins and three fulling tubs (BCTH 1912: 494)

properties.name: fullonica (rooms 8, 9 and 10)
properties.plan_source: Amraoui 2020a: 134, fig. 4.11; Amraoui 2020b: 235, fig. 11.10; Christofle's plan of the fullery in Wilson 2001: 274, fig. 12.01; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026)
properties.description: the fullery that fills the whole north-east quarter of the block, rooms 8, 9 and 10 with the eleven compartments a to k, eight of them with tubs still in place, two with the tubs missing and one, k, with no tub at all on Amraoui's plan, plus a tub standing free in room 9, and the well in room 10, the largest fulling workshop in Timgad, which she says had no room for anything but fulling and must have done the finishing on an upper floor, and was completely unconnected to the rest of the block (Amraoui 2020a: 134-135, fig. 4.11; 2020b: 234, fig. 11.10), so probable as a whole, since the plans agree on every bit of it and the ground backs its walls; it's the establishment Christofle planned with ten tubs A to J and the well W (Wilson 2001: 274, fig. 12.01, after Christoflé 1935: 77), matched to this corner by its tubs, its well and its paved passage

properties.name: first shop, with its back room (south-east corner)
properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47; Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026)
properties.description: the shop with a back room at the south-east corner of the main block, the first of the five independent shops Ballu lists along the south front from the east (1922: 47), with its street door and the door into the back room on his plan; Ballu says the five shops were entirely independent, with their floors 1.20 m above the house's (1922: 47)

properties.name: second shop, with its back room
properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47; Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026)
properties.description: the second shop with a back room in Ballu's list from the east, after the narrow corridor and the secondary entrance (1922: 47), placed here by that order; the two porch columns drawn in front of its door don't fit his text, which gives the porch on two columns to the secondary entrance (1923: 46)

properties.name: third shop
properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47; Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026)
properties.description: the third shop in Ballu's list, the one just east of the main entrance (1922: 47), placed by that order, with only its front room since the room behind it opens on the vestibule

properties.name: fourth shop, with its annex
properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47; Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026)
properties.description: the fourth shop with its annex in Ballu's list, west of the main entrance (1922: 47), placed by that order; his remise with a door of 2.05 m and second antechamber, which come between the main entrance and this shop in his list, might be the room west of the stepped corridor with its wide opening on the vestibule, so I've placed the shop by his order and the match isn't certain ??; he says the last two were in poor shape (1922: 47)

properties.name: fifth shop, with its small room behind (south-west corner)
properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47; Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026)
properties.description: the fifth shop at the south-west corner of the main block with the small room behind it, Ballu's last in his list (1922: 47), and the stair room north of that small room fits where he puts the stair cage, north of the fifth shop's back room (1922: 48); he says the last two were in poor shape (1922: 47)

properties.name: grain store with four stone troughs (wheat)
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1911a (Sept années): 74, plan of the house, with his description 72-73 (first published in his report on the 1906 excavations, Ballu 1907: 261-262); round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026), set on the walls as the imagery shows them
properties.description: the room where Ballu found four stone troughs along the north wall, not drawn as a fixture here, covered with bits of plaster, concrete and earth and full of wheat blackened by fire with the grains still whole (1911a: 72); paved in sandstone and reached from the sandstone room south of it; drawn as a store on his word, probable

properties.name: grain store (barley)
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1911a (Sept années): 74, plan of the house, with his description 72-73 (first published in his report on the 1906 excavations, Ballu 1907: 261-262); round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026), set on the walls as the imagery shows them
properties.description: the room north-east of the central corridor and west of the troughs room, where Ballu found barley kept the same way (1911a: 72); he says it was about the same size as the troughs room, though it comes out a good deal bigger as the ground puts the wall between them; drawn as a store on his word, probable

properties.name: potter's kiln over the north-west corner of mosaic 190 (later)
properties.plan_source: Germain 1969: 125-127 (nos 190-192), the room sizes and what the inscription faced; not on Meunier's plan (Germain 1969: 122, fig. 17; Rebuffat 1974: pl. 'Thamugadi 12'); round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: the potter's kiln that Germain says was put in at a later period and damaged the north-west corner of mosaic 190 (1969: 126); he gives no plan of it, so this is a notional square at the north-west corner of the west portico, where the mosaic's north-west corner would be; nothing shows on the ground and it's uncertain, drawn so the later workshop use of the house is on the map

properties.name: dye-works room in the south-west corner (two basins, two terracotta tubs)
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 495 (BCTH; offprint p. 33), the room as Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 draw it; round-2 drawing (Oct 5, 2026)
properties.description: the south-west corner room of the west half, which Ballu says held two basins, one of them quite big, and two terracotta tubs (*une chambre contenant deux bassins, dont un assez grand, et deux cuves de terre cuite*, a room with two basins, one fairly large, and two terracotta tubs, BCTH 1912: 495), in a building he says was used by two dyers (*deux industriels en teinturerie*, BCTH 1912: 494); he doesn't say where in the room they stood and I can't make anything out on the ground, so only the room is drawn; Wilson stipples it as a room where fulling or dyeing went on (2001: 279, fig. 12.08), and reads the Timgad works as mainly fulleries (2001: 275); probable

properties.name: basin room of the east half's dye-works, the big south-east room
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 495 (BCTH; offprint p. 33), the room as Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 draw it; round-2 drawing (Oct 5, 2026)
properties.description: the big south-east room, the only room of the east half on the south street, so it's likely Ballu's room with a single basin on that street (*une troisième possédant un seul bassin (sur la rue sud, c'est-à-dire le cinquième Decumanus)*, a third with only one basin, on the south street, that is the fifth *decumanus*, BCTH 1912: 495), one of the rooms of the east half's dye-works; Courtois and Wilson both draw it as one room, and Wilson stipples it (2001: 279, fig. 12.08); probable

properties.name: dye-works, the row of rooms on the fifth *decumanus* (east-west street)
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31), the room as Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 draw it; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: the row of rooms along the fifth *decumanus* (east-west street) where Ballu puts the north half's dye-works (he says there were two dyers, *teinturiers*, in the house), a room paved in stone with a well and three terracotta vats for dyeing (*trois cuves de terre cuite pour la teinture*), two basins for the same work and three other rooms, all opening onto the street (BCTH 1912: 493); he doesn't say which room is the paved one, so this takes in the whole row, the way Wilson stipples it (2001: 279, fig. 12.08); his vats here are for dyeing where the south half's are fulling vats, though Amraoui reads Ballu's Timgad dye-works as fulleries (2020a: 129-130) and Wilson the Timgad establishments as mainly fulleries (2001: 275); probable

properties.name: fullery (fullonica), the paved room east of the central wall in the south half
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31), the room as Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 draw it; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: the long room on the east side of the south half's north row, Ballu's paved room with a well, two basins and four fulling vats (*quatre cuves à foulon*) separated by masonry partitions (BCTH 1912: 493); Courtois and Wilson both draw the room, and Wilson stipples it as a room where fulling went on (2001: 279, fig. 12.08); probable

properties.name: storeroom (magasin) in the south-east corner
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31), the room as Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 draw it; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026)
properties.description: the vast storeroom (*vaste magasin*) Ballu puts in the south-east corner of the block (BCTH 1912: 493), the room east of the short wall up from the south wall, about 6 by 5 m inside; probable

properties.name: workshop, the west part's paved east-west room (two vats)
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31), the rooms as Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 draw them and the satellite imagery shows them; round-2 drawing (Oct 13, 2026)
properties.description: the room along the fifth *decumanus* (east-west street) in the west half of the block, which Ballu gives as one east-west room paved in stone with two vats (*la pièce est-ouest, dallée en pierre et possédant deux cuves*, the east-west room, paved in stone and with two vats, BCTH 1912: 493, offprint p. 31); the plans and the ground split it in two, so this covers both, the west and second rooms of the south row; he doesn't say what the vats were for, but there were two craftsmen in the block (*deux industriels*) and fulling vessels in the east half, so probable

properties.name: workshop, the east part's east-west room (a basin and a terracotta vat)
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31), the rooms as Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 draw them and the satellite imagery shows them; round-2 drawing (Oct 13, 2026)
properties.description: the room along the fifth *decumanus* (east-west street) in the east half, Ballu's east-west room with a basin and a terracotta vat (*la pièce est-ouest avec un bassin et une cuve en terre cuite*, the east-west room with a basin and a terracotta vat, BCTH 1912: 493, offprint p. 31); the plans and the ground split it in two, so this covers both, the third and east rooms of the south row; probable

properties.name: fullery (fullonica), the east part's 15 m room (a well and two large fulling vessels)
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 493 (BCTH; offprint p. 31), the rooms as Courtois 1951 and Wilson 2001 draw them and the satellite imagery shows them; round-2 drawing (Oct 13, 2026)
properties.description: the long room on the west side of the east half, between Ballu's median wall and the wall between the fourth and east rooms, from his east-west wall to the boulevard, which he gives as one room of 15 m with a well and two large fulling vessels (*une salle de 15 mètres, avec un puits et deux grands vases de foulon*, a room of 15 m with a well and two large fulling vessels, BCTH 1912: 493, offprint p. 31); it comes out about 14.7 m long between the wall lines on the ground, so it fits, but the plans divide it into five rooms with cross walls and the wall between its third and fourth rooms, and the ground into six with the faint wall in the second row, so this covers all of them, the third and fourth rooms of the second, third and north rows; probable
